title: Define the durable storage adapter contract
objective: Define the adapter contract that maps @earendil-works/pi-durable storage to Rivet Actor SQLite without weakening the actor single-writer invariant.
acceptanceCriteria: A written storage mapping identifies every Pi Durable record and its Rivet ownership.
The adapter keeps all writes within one Rivet Actor's SQLite single-writer boundary.
A minimal conformance fixture can reopen and read the same committed conversation state.
New production SQLite reads have query-efficiency coverage where required by repository policy.
Migration and rollback conditions are explicit.
constraints: Do not replace the existing AgentSession actor API.
Do not replay model or tool work in this issue.
Current @rivet-dev/pi stores actor header, entries, settings, and sandbox identity in actor SQLite; one actor generation owns one live AgentSession and serializes entries in append order.
The application supplies credentials, an active run is aborted on sleep or destroy, and the current integration persists a transcript rather than in-flight work.
Durable mode is a separate opt-in actor surface for conversations, entries, documents, submissions, and tasks; existing @rivet-dev/pi behavior remains the compatibility baseline.
No task may be exposed before its durable state commits, and a process restart must not silently replay a potentially mutating tool.

Supervisor correction from the rejected first draft: durable ownership belongs to the stable Rivet Actor and its SQLite database across generations. The currently active actor generation holds the exclusive writer lease; a restart or wake creates a new generation of the same actor that must reacquire and read the previously committed state.

The reopen conformance fixture must close one actor generation and verify a new generation of the same actor reacquires identical committed state. Never describe restart as reopening the same generation.
Treat integrations/pi/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and integrations/pi/docs/ROADMAP.md as the governing references summarized above.
This case produces a reviewable contract, not code changes.
